plan.title: Gender Improvement Comparison
plan.subtitle: Comparing baseline to endline performance metrics by gender

panels.title: Total Girls
panels.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM "baseline" WHERE "Gender" = 'Female'

panels.title: Total Boys
panels.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM "baseline" WHERE "Gender" = 'Male'

panels.title: Avg Height Change (cm) by Gender
panels.sql: SELECT b."Gender", AVG(e."Height cm" - b."Height cm") AS height_change FROM "baseline" b JOIN "endline" e ON b."Child ID" = e."Child ID" GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Avg Sit-ups Change by Gender
panels.sql: SELECT b."Gender", AVG(e."Sit ups" - b."Sit ups") AS situp_change FROM "baseline" b JOIN "endline" e ON b."Child ID" = e."Child ID" GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Avg Shuttle Run Improvement (sec) by Gender
panels.sql: SELECT b."Gender", AVG(b."Shuttle run sec" - e."Shuttle run sec") AS shuttle_improvement FROM "baseline" b JOIN "endline" e ON b."Child ID" = e."Child ID" GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

plan.narrative:
To determine if girls and boys are improving equally, we compare the average change in key physical metrics from baseline to endline for each gender.

The average height increase for {{p3.1}} was {{p3.height_change}} cm, while {{p3.2}} saw an average increase of {{p3.height_change}} cm. This indicates that {{p3.1}} had a greater average growth in height.

In terms of core strength, {{p4.1}} improved their average sit-ups by {{p4.situp_change}}, compared to {{p4.2}} who improved by {{p4.situp_change}}. {{p4.1}} showed a larger gain in this metric.

For agility, measured by the shuttle run, a lower time is better. {{p5.1}} improved their time by {{p5.shuttle_improvement}} seconds on average, while {{p5.2}} improved by {{p5.shuttle_improvement}} seconds. {{p5.1}} demonstrated a greater improvement in speed/agility.
